test_suite: B2P Batter Risk Model - Validation Dataset v1.0
description: 20 test cases covering fresh, borderline, spoiled, fridge-stored, and sales-velocity scenarios

test_cases.description: Fresh batch, room temp, fast sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~4.5. Very fresh. Fast turnover guarantees it sells before any souring.

test_cases.description: Fresh batch, room temp, slow sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~4.4. Still fresh despite slow sales. 6 hours is not enough to spoil.

test_cases.description: 12 hours old, room temp, average sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~4.1. Getting tangy but still safe and tasty.

test_cases.description: 18 hours old, room temp, slow sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~3.9. Crossing into 'sour' territory. Needs to sell today.

test_cases.description: 24 hours old, room temp, average sales (The Borderline)
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH exactly 3.5. Classic 24-hour mark. Sell immediately.

test_cases.description: 24 hours old, room temp, very fast sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH 3.5, but 95% already sold. Business risk is LOW because it's almost gone.

test_cases.description: 30 hours old, room temp, average sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~3.3. Oversoured. Quality is compromised.

test_cases.description: 36 hours old, room temp, fast sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~3.1. Definitely spoiled, but fast sales might clear the remaining stock.

test_cases.description: 48 hours old, room temp (The Dead Zone)
test_cases.scientific_reason: pH ~2.9. Completely fermented. Unsellable.

test_cases.description: 12 hours old, HOT weather (32°C), average sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: 32°C accelerates fermentation. 12 hours feels like 18 hours at room temp.

test_cases.description: 18 hours old, HOT weather (32°C), slow sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: Heat + time + slow movement = guaranteed spoilage.

test_cases.description: 24 hours old, HOT weather (32°C), fast sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: Even with fast sales, 24 hours at 32°C is chemically spoiled.

test_cases.description: 24 hours old, FRIDGE (4°C), slow sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: Fridge pauses fermentation. pH is still ~4.4. Perfectly fine.

test_cases.description: 48 hours old, FRIDGE (4°C), average sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: 48 hours in fridge = ~5-6 hours at room temp. pH ~4.1. Edible but getting old.

test_cases.description: 72 hours old, FRIDGE (4°C), slow sales
test_cases.scientific_reason: 3 days in fridge. pH ~3.8. It's turning sour even in cold storage.

test_cases.description: Extreme Cold (0°C) - Freezer, 24 hours
test_cases.scientific_reason: Fermentation is almost completely halted at 0°C. pH ~4.5.

test_cases.description: Extreme Heat (40°C) - Truck left in sun, 8 hours
test_cases.scientific_reason: 40°C accelerates fermentation 4x. 8 hours feels like 32 hours at room temp.

test_cases.description: Vendor with super-fast turnover (sell_rate 1.0), old batch
test_cases.scientific_reason: Even though it's 30 hours old, a sell-rate of 1.0 means it's already finished (or selling instantly). Business risk is zero.

test_cases.description: Vendor with dead stock (sell_rate 0.01), moderately old
test_cases.scientific_reason: Only 15 hours old (still chemically low), but literally no one is buying. It will sit there and spoil tomorrow.

test_cases.description: The 'Perfect' batch (Fresh + Cold + Fast)
test_cases.scientific_reason: Just made, kept cold, selling like hotcakes. Perfect inventory.
